synthesizedFacts.fact: Weeping eczema is a form of eczema characterized by fluid-filled blisters that ooze clear or yellowish fluid.
Weeping eczema can be triggered by infections such as bacterial (Staphylococcus aureus), viral (herpes simplex), or fungal infections.
Weeping eczema is not inherently contagious, but the infections that cause it can be.
Treatment for weeping eczema includes corticosteroids, antihistamines, and immunosuppressive medications.
Weeping eczema can lead to a yellow or honey-colored crust as the fluid dries.
